title: The World of Warhammer: the Official Illustrated Guide - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_OsQEaApgwY

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a browse through *The World of Warhammer: The Official Illustrated Guide*, a 1996 encyclopedia of the Old World compiled by Richard Wolfrick Galland — a book he came to late, having played 40K rather than Warhammer Fantasy Battle in his youth. He frames it as an ideal primer for anyone whose Old World knowledge comes mostly from Warhammer Quest and Advanced HeroQuest: race by race — Lizardmen, High Elves, Dwarfs, the Empire, the Realms of Chaos, Skaven, Undead — with home territories, runes, beliefs and battle plans, all wrapped in glorious John Blanche-era artwork. He delights in the Chaos gods, the Skaven's under-empire, the metal-as-hell Undead splash pages, and reflects on how deeply Lovecraftian cosmic horror seeped into the setting's very origins. But he returns repeatedly to one damning flaw: for a book that calls itself an *illustrated* guide, it credits not a single artist — a real disservice to the people whose images made the Old World sing. Recommended lore, with an asterisk.
